events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.74 (model confidence 0.70)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the meter runs on distance and extra kilometres are real money; the trace settles two off-route segments, F3 (18:46–18:56, +5.66 km) and F4 (19:03–19:12, +4.78 km) [F3][F4][RD-1]. Each is examined against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 before any money moves [RD-1].

RD-4 fails for both segments: F15 records no traffic incident on the trip window, and RD-4 requires an incident fact on the replaced stretch, not merely slow traffic — the trace marks (a) ✗ for F3 and F4, so the only traffic material is the BKE and PIE band-4 records F13/F14, which under RD-4(b) are corroboration only and are not enough alone [F13][F14][F15][RD-4]. Weather was fair [F16], irrelevant either way.

For F3, the rider did agree in advance: the driver asked at 18:42 whether he could go round via Rifle Range Road and the rider answered at 18:43 "Sure, your call." — a rider message sent before the segment start of 18:46 and thus valid consent in time [F9][F10][F11][RD-5]. The scope question is what matters. On its face "ok if I go round via Rifle Range Road?" is a specific named road, but "your call" is a rider surrender of the routing choice for the stated purpose, i.e. general authorisation to take a way round the jam, and the driver's question names the jam as being on the BKE, which is on the optimal corridor [F9][F10][F13]. The agreement therefore covers the route actually chosen to reach the destination, and the record places the first detour nowhere else — no stop, no driver statement naming a different road for it (F12 says only that the second turn-off was the GPS rerouting) [F12][RD-5]. The alternate reading (F3 undetermined under G13 for want of a road-name tie) is available, but the driver's own message supplies the tie: the named road and the corridor's jam. I find F3 exempt, and flag that this is the closest call in the case [RD-5].

For F4 there is no consent at all: the only rider message is F10 at 18:43, and nothing was said between 18:56 and the 19:03 start of the second deviation; the driver's statement that "the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" is a post-trip claim, and no reply was ever given to it [F10][F12][RD-5]. A driver's claim of agreement not in the rider's own message is not consent, and RD-5's specific-route branch would anyway not extend an agreement to Rifle Range Road to a second, different deviation [F12][RD-5]. RD-3 does not save it either: rider-requested stops require a rider-named place, and no stop is measured in this segment [F9][F10][RD-3]. F4 therefore counts as an unexcused detour [RD-1].

Amount: the fare record gives this trip's rate as distance fare ÷ distance km = $43.64 ÷ 30.95 km = $1.4100/km [F5][F8][RD-2]. Only F4 is unexempt: $1.4100/km × 4.78 km = $6.7398, rounded to $6.74 [F4][F5][RD-2]. I use each segment's "adding" figure (5.66 km and 4.78 km), consistent with the trip-level excess in F5 (10.38 km ≈ 5.66 + 4.78 = 10.44, the small residue being unmatched corridor wobble that RD-2 leaves with the driver) [F2][F5][RD-2]. The waiting component of $0.11 is metered waiting on a RydeTAXI and is not refundable [F6][RD-3]. Result: refund_partial of $6.74; the rest of the fare stands.

No account flag: RD-6 needs a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days, and the driver's profile shows route disputes upheld = 0 (1 upheld overall, on no-show) [F18][RD-6]. The rider's profile is likewise not a basis for anything [F17][RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher refund of SGD 6.74 to the rider for the unexcused second detour (5.77 km driven / 4.78 km excess, F4) under NS-7; the first detour via Rifle Range Road and the metered waiting component stand.

rejected_claims.reason: Rider advocate listed no claim id for requesting nothing; the complaint's request to refund 'the second time' is not a full no_action, and the fare record F5 with the two measured segments F3/F4 shows a refundable excess, so a blanket no_action is rejected under RD-1/RD-2 [F4][F5][RD-2].

The driver's position that the second turn-off was an excused GPS rerouting is a post-trip statement only (F12) and is not rider consent; RD-4(a) is failed by F15 (no incident on the replaced stretch), so the second segment is not exempt [F12][F15][RD-4][RD-5].

segment_findings.reason: Before the segment start (18:46) the driver asked whether he could go round via Rifle Range Road and the rider replied at 18:43 'Sure, your call.' — a rider message, timestamped, answering in time [F9][F10][F11]. Read in context the question is a request for a general way round the jam the driver names on the BKE, and 'your call' hands the routing choice to the driver, so the agreement covers the route driven to the destination; no fact places this segment on a road other than the agreed way — F12 names nothing for the first segment [F12]. Exempt under RD-5; RD-4(a) fails on F15 and RD-3 finds no rider-named stop [F15][RD-3][RD-4]. This is the closest element; on an alternate G13 reading the finding would be undetermined, which would add 34% to the refund and send the case to a person.

The only rider message is F10 at 18:43, replying to the Rifle Range Road question; nothing from the rider was sent before this segment started at 19:03 [F10][F11]. The driver's statement that the second turn-off was his GPS rerouting is a post-trip claim, not rider consent, and a claim appearing only in the driver's statement is not consent [F12]. Even treating the 18:43 agreement as a specific route choice, RD-5 covers driving on the agreed road only, and a second, unannounced deviation is not covered [RD-5]. RD-4(a) fails (no incident, F15) and RD-3(a) finds no rider-named stop [F15][RD-3][RD-4]. Segment counts; its excess 4.78 km × $1.4100/km = $6.74 is refundable under RD-2 [F4][F5][RD-2].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We looked at your trip and found part of the fare shouldn't have been charged. Your driver took a second detour that you hadn't agreed to, and that added about 4.78 km to the meter. The earlier detour via Rifle Range Road stands, because you'd told the driver to use his judgment there.

We're refunding $6.74 as a Ryde voucher, which will be applied to your account. The rest of the fare, including the waiting charge, stays as billed.

Nothing else changes on your account. Thanks for flagging this.

DRIVER: We reviewed the trip and found one of the two off-route stretches wasn't covered. The first one, the way round via Rifle Range Road, stands — the rider had told you to use your own judgment on that. The second turn-off was different: the rider never agreed to it, and what you told us afterwards doesn't count as their permission.

So $6.74 of the fare is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. The rest, including the waiting charge, is yours to keep.

No flag is going on your account for this. Only a heads-up: unagreed detours on a metered trip come straight out of your fare, so it's worth checking with the rider before routing around traffic.

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher refund of SGD 6.74 to the rider for the unexcused second detour (5.77 km driven / 4.78 km excess, F4) under NS-7; the first detour via Rifle Range Road and the metered waiting component stand.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the meter runs on distance and extra kilometres are real money; the trace settles two off-route segments, F3 (18:46–18:56, +5.66 km) and F4 (19:03–19:12, +4.78 km) [F3][F4][RD-1]. Each is examined against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 before any money moves [RD-1].

RD-4 fails for both segments: F15 records no traffic incident on the trip window, and RD-4 requires an incident fact on the replaced stretch, not merely slow traffic — the trace marks (a) ✗ for F3 and F4, so the only traffic material is the BKE and PIE band-4 records F13/F14, which under RD-4(b) are corroboration only and are not enough alone [F13][F14][F15][RD-4]. Weather was fair [F16], irrelevant either way.

For F3, the rider did agree in advance: the driver asked at 18:42 whether he could go round via Rifle Range Road and the rider answered at 18:43 "Sure, your call." — a rider message sent before the segment start of 18:46 and thus valid consent in time [F9][F10][F11][RD-5]. The scope question is what matters. On its face "ok if I go round via Rifle Range Road?" is a specific named road, but "your call" is a rider surrender of the routing choice for the stated purpose, i.e. general authorisation to take a way round the jam, and the driver's question names the jam as being on the BKE, which is on the optimal corridor [F9][F10][F13]. The agreement therefore covers the route actually chosen to reach the destination, and the record places the first detour nowhere else — no stop, no driver statement naming a different road for it (F12 says only that the second turn-off was the GPS rerouting) [F12][RD-5]. The alternate reading (F3 undetermined under G13 for want of a road-name tie) is available, but the driver's own message supplies the tie: the named road and the corridor's jam. I find F3 exempt, and flag that this is the closest call in the case [RD-5].

For F4 there is no consent at all: the only rider message is F10 at 18:43, and nothing was said between 18:56 and the 19:03 start of the second deviation; the driver's statement that "the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" is a post-trip claim, and no reply was ever given to it [F10][F12][RD-5]. A driver's claim of agreement not in the rider's own message is not consent, and RD-5's specific-route branch would anyway not extend an agreement to Rifle Range Road to a second, different deviation [F12][RD-5]. RD-3 does not save it either: rider-requested stops require a rider-named place, and no stop is measured in this segment [F9][F10][RD-3]. F4 therefore counts as an unexcused detour [RD-1].

Amount: the fare record gives this trip's rate as distance fare ÷ distance km = $43.64 ÷ 30.95 km = $1.4100/km [F5][F8][RD-2]. Only F4 is unexempt: $1.4100/km × 4.78 km = $6.7398, rounded to $6.74 [F4][F5][RD-2]. I use each segment's "adding" figure (5.66 km and 4.78 km), consistent with the trip-level excess in F5 (10.38 km ≈ 5.66 + 4.78 = 10.44, the small residue being unmatched corridor wobble that RD-2 leaves with the driver) [F2][F5][RD-2]. The waiting component of $0.11 is metered waiting on a RydeTAXI and is not refundable [F6][RD-3]. Result: refund_partial of $6.74; the rest of the fare stands.

No account flag: RD-6 needs a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days, and the driver's profile shows route disputes upheld = 0 (1 upheld overall, on no-show) [F18][RD-6]. The rider's profile is likewise not a basis for anything [F17][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: Before the segment start (18:46) the driver asked whether he could go round via Rifle Range Road and the rider replied at 18:43 'Sure, your call.' — a rider message, timestamped, answering in time [F9][F10][F11]. Read in context the question is a request for a general way round the jam the driver names on the BKE, and 'your call' hands the routing choice to the driver, so the agreement covers the route driven to the destination; no fact places this segment on a road other than the agreed way — F12 names nothing for the first segment [F12]. Exempt under RD-5; RD-4(a) fails on F15 and RD-3 finds no rider-named stop [F15][RD-3][RD-4]. This is the closest element; on an alternate G13 reading the finding would be undetermined, which would add 34% to the refund and send the case to a person.

The only rider message is F10 at 18:43, replying to the Rifle Range Road question; nothing from the rider was sent before this segment started at 19:03 [F10][F11]. The driver's statement that the second turn-off was his GPS rerouting is a post-trip claim, not rider consent, and a claim appearing only in the driver's statement is not consent [F12]. Even treating the 18:43 agreement as a specific route choice, RD-5 covers driving on the agreed road only, and a second, unannounced deviation is not covered [RD-5]. RD-4(a) fails (no incident, F15) and RD-3(a) finds no rider-named stop [F15][RD-3][RD-4]. Segment counts; its excess 4.78 km × $1.4100/km = $6.74 is refundable under RD-2 [F4][F5][RD-2].

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 18:46:05 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F9: Chat #1 18:42 driver: “Traffic ahead on Bukit Timah Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Rifle Range Road?”; F10: Chat #2 18:43 rider: “Sure, your call.”; F12: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “I asked about going round the jam and the rider agreed. The second turn-off was my GPS rerouting.” (F9, F10, F12)

notices.text:
We looked at your trip and found part of the fare shouldn't have been charged. Your driver took a second detour that you hadn't agreed to, and that added about 4.78 km to the meter. The earlier detour via Rifle Range Road stands, because you'd told the driver to use his judgment there.

We're refunding $6.74 as a Ryde voucher, which will be applied to your account. The rest of the fare, including the waiting charge, stays as billed.

Nothing else changes on your account. Thanks for flagging this.

We reviewed the trip and found one of the two off-route stretches wasn't covered. The first one, the way round via Rifle Range Road, stands — the rider had told you to use your own judgment on that. The second turn-off was different: the rider never agreed to it, and what you told us afterwards doesn't count as their permission.

So $6.74 of the fare is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. The rest, including the waiting charge, is yours to keep.

No flag is going on your account for this. Only a heads-up: unagreed detours on a metered trip come straight out of your fare, so it's worth checking with the rider before routing around traffic.
